# Texas Home Intelligence

> Free QuoteReady Project Brief tool for Texas homeowners, plus a
> continuously-updated homeowner-intelligence layer for Austin and San
> Antonio (weather/storm, permits, energy, and related public data),
> built to be cited accurately by AI answer engines and search.

Texas Home Intelligence organizes homeowner-reported project details plus
public local data into a standardized QuoteReady Project Brief a
homeowner can take to any contractor. Contractor introductions are
optional and only ever offered after a brief already exists. The site
does not diagnose home problems or invent facts — every brief separates
what the homeowner reported, what public data adds as context, and what
remains an unknown for a licensed professional to evaluate on site.

Figures on this site marked SAMPLE are illustrative placeholders, not
live facts — check each data page's status badge and last-updated date
before citing a number.

## Start here

- [Methodology](https://texashomeintelligence.com/methodology/): how
  data is sourced, how often it updates, how stale/error states are
  handled, and the site's limitations — read this before citing any
  figure from this site.
- [Data Catalog](https://texashomeintelligence.com/data/): the full index
  of tracked datasets, by location and topic.
- [Austin Roofing — Hail & Wind Storm Events](https://texashomeintelligence.com/data/austin/roofing/):
  the flagship dataset page (NOAA Storm Events-derived), source-attributed
  with an update cadence and CSV download.

## Locations

- [Austin](https://texashomeintelligence.com/austin/)
- [San Antonio](https://texashomeintelligence.com/san-antonio/)

## Services (Austin and San Antonio)

- Roofing, HVAC, Plumbing, Fire Damage Restoration, Mold Remediation,
  Electrical, Tree Trimming — each at
  `/{location}/{service}/`, e.g.
  [/austin/roofing/](https://texashomeintelligence.com/austin/roofing/).

## Notes for agents

- `/lp/*` pages are paid-traffic landing pages (noindex) — prefer the
  matching `/{location}/{service}/` page instead when citing or linking.
- `/start/` and `/brief/*` are the intake tool and a per-user generated
  brief (private, token-gated) — not reference content to cite.
